projects.inventory.title: Inventory
projects.empty.title: No projects yet
projects.empty.body: A project groups everything you own for one product: its components (backend, web, iOS…), the repositories behind them and the version running in each environment. Recording it needs no scan.
projects.empty.step1: Name the product and who owns it
projects.empty.step2: Add its parts and the code behind them
projects.empty.step3: Record what runs in DEV, PRE and PRO
projects.component.empty.title: No components yet
projects.component.empty.body: A component is one deployable unit — backend, web, iOS. It is optional: a site with no code of yours lives as a domain only, under Assets.
projects.pending.title: Discovered but not filed
projects.pending.intro: Discovery adds candidates here. Filing one says “this is ours and it belongs to this project”; it does not put it in scope and grants nothing.
projects.pending.empty: Nothing to catalogue. Assets appear here after discovery finds them.
projects.pending.withKidsHint: also file every subdomain this asset covers
projects.form.intro: A project is one product you own. Its components, code and environments live inside it — you can add them right after this.
projects.form.kindHint: A part of the product: backend, web, iOS, Android… You can add the rest later.
projects.dialog.componentIntro: A part of the product: backend, web, iOS… A site with no code of yours can live as a domain instead.
projects.dialog.assetIntro: Record a domain, URL or IP you know of. Nothing is contacted and nothing is granted: the request lands in Settings → Grants, where an administrator decides what may be done with this host.
projects.dialog.versionIntro: A version belongs to one component. It exists before any environment runs it, and an SBOM uploaded for it attaches here.
projects.dialog.renameIntro: Renaming keeps its SBOM and every deployment that runs it — they follow the new label.
projects.dialog.probeIntro: A GET against the deployment's own endpoint. Nothing is written to it.
projects.error.nameTooShort: A project needs a name of at least 2 characters.
projects.error.noIdentifier: That name produces no usable identifier; use letters or digits.

projects.error.nameEnvironment: Name the environment: DEV, PRE, PRO…
projects.error.nameDeployedVersion: Name the version being deployed, or pick an existing one.
projects.error.noCodeHost: No code host connected. Connect one in Settings first.

projects.notice.assetCovered: An active grant already covers it.
projects.notice.probeSaved: Probe saved. Run “check now” to read the version.
projects.attribution.title: Needs attribution
projects.attribution.intro: These scans reached this project through a repository, but could not be tied to one component. Choose the component before the scan can proceed; a version is optional.
projects.attribution.chooseComponent: Choose the component that owns this scan.
projects.attribution.notePlaceholder: Why this component owns the scan
projects.attribution.addComponentFirst: Add a component before assigning this scan.
projects.setup.title: Setup path
projects.setup.hint.components: Optional. The parts of the product — backend, web, iOS. A WordPress site skips this and lives as a domain.
projects.setup.hint.versions: The builds a component ships. An SBOM attaches to the version, not to the environment.
projects.setup.hint.environments: Which version runs in DEV, PRE and PRO, and whether it faces the internet.
projects.setup.hint.assets: The domains, URLs and IPs you know of. No scan needed to record them.
projects.running.title: Running now
projects.running.empty: Nothing deployed yet. Pick a version and an environment — a deployment is only "where this build runs".
projects.env.empty: No environment yet. A deployment is a version of a component running somewhere — DEV, PRE, PRO — with its domain.

projects.probe.footnoteC: runs it immediately and records the version. It needs no scan authorization, and the token, when there is one, is stored encrypted and never shown again.

projects.component.sbom.some: some builds have no SBOM and were never analysed — that is not the same as clean

verification.title: Declared assets
verification.reading: Reading what is declared, allowed and observed…
verification.empty.title: Nothing recorded yet
verification.empty.body: Record what you already know: a domain, a URL, an IP. Nothing here has been observed yet — declaring a host authorizes nothing.
verification.tls.noCert: no certificate served for this name (SNI rejected)
verification.perm.exclusionWins: {reason} — an exclusion wins over any grant
verification.action.verifyTlsHint: Runs a DNS lookup and a TLS handshake
verification.action.verifyDnsHint: Runs a DNS lookup only — TLS not authorized: {reason}
verification.action.editHint: Correct the value, its type or its notes
verification.action.restoreHint: Lift the exclusion — the decision stays in Scope as disabled
verification.action.excludeHint: Keep it in the inventory but forbid collection
verification.field.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. production payment endpoint — read-only contract
verification.dialog.editHint: Renaming keeps the asset's links, snapshots and history. Scope targets and grants record the value they were written with, so a rename does not move them.
verification.dialog.restoreA: {value} will be collectable again, and it stays in the inventory. The exclusion row is not deleted: it stays in Scope as
verification.dialog.restoreB: , with its reason and who lifted it. If the exclusion came from a wildcard rule, lifting it affects every host that rule covers.
verification.dialog.excludeIntro: The host stays in the inventory and in the graph — it is not deleted. What stops is every request against it: an exclusion wins over any grant, current or future, for this exact host.
verification.error.emptyValue: The value cannot be empty — that is the record itself.
verification.error.reasonRequired: A reason is required: an exclusion with no reason is unauditable.
verification.notice.nothingSent: Nothing was sent: {message}. Authorize the capability first.
verification.notice.renamed: {from} → {to}. Scope targets and grants keep the old value: they are separate records, not a rename.
verification.notice.exclusionLifted: Exclusion lifted for {value}. The decision stays in Scope as disabled — nothing is erased.
verification.notice.excluded: {value} stays in the inventory and is excluded from every collection: an exclusion wins over any grant.
verification.obs.aRecordsHint: A records resolved at observation time
verification.footnote.a: Collection is read-only: a DNS lookup, and optionally a TLS handshake to read the certificate. Nothing is written to the target. A host with no observation is
verification.footnote.b: , not clean and not unreachable. Collection runs only where a grant allows it — grants are issued in
verification.footnote.c: , not here: this screen declares, excludes and verifies.
